Definition: A piping design engine with a full internal solver used for design iteration that produces handoff-ready model data for downstream professional validation; the new product identity.
Notes: New product framing replacing the standalone open-source stress platform identity.

Definition: The richer schema-backed source-of-truth layer including geometry, components, supports, constraints, equipment interfaces, provenance, unresolved assumptions, and design intent.
The idealized solver-ready representation derived from the physical model.

The target-specific export representation; the handoff package contains canonical model data, units manifest, entity IDs, library/rule references, unresolved assumptions, warnings, hashes, and target mapping metadata.
Notes: One of three model layers; export-side artifact.

Definition: First-class product scope covering line lists, P&ID connectivity, equipment/nozzle locations, pipe specs, routing corridors, no-go volumes, rack elevations, supportable zones, valve access, slope/drain/vent, clearance envelopes, construction constraints, owner preferences, and stress-review triggers.

Engine for connectivity, endpoint matching, supportable span ranges, clearance envelopes, no-go volumes, slope requirements, drain/vent logic, valve access zones, supportable structure zones, and missing required data.
A named, immutable snapshot of a model at a point in time.
A solver execution attached to a specific model state, bound to solver version, settings, units, load cases, and rule-pack/library references.
A deterministic diff between two model states and/or two analysis runs using stable IDs, manual mappings, unit-normalized quantities, and tolerance profiles.
An accepted professional stress-analysis platform used outside OpenPipeStress to validate results for project reliance.
The basis defining the product boundary: OpenPipeStress computes and helps design, the prover tool validates for reliance, and the responsible engineer accepts.
Notes: Boundary is defined by claim authority, not solver capability.

Definition: A structured, schema- and constraint-validated change to the model, shown as a diff and requiring user acceptance; categories include add_route_segment, move_node, insert_bend, add_support.
Nodes with six degrees of freedom retained as a core solver commitment in MVP.
User-supplied private rule packs with non-code examples; private-by-default with provenance metadata.
Design-knowledge volumes representing space where routing/supports are not allowed.
Design-knowledge corridors guiding pipe routing, consumed by route/support generation.
Manifest of canonical model export including model hash, units manifest, entity ID manifest, library/rule references, warnings, unresolved assumptions, and target mapping metadata.
Local-first data storage/operation retained and added to MVP.
